title: The Crab Derby, 2013
logline: Twenty-ninth annual. Maria, eight months along, letters it herself because Wood's asleep and Gully's on the water. Wood wakes to find it done and better.

panels.composition: Gully's, afternoon. MARIA, very pregnant, in the county rain shell, at the counter with the flyer and a marker. The girl, three, under the counter with the old dog. GULLY absent — on the water.

image.prompt: a heavily pregnant woman in a county rain shell lettering a flyer at a bait-shop counter while a three-year-old and an old dog sit beneath it, razor-sharp ink

panels.composition: Her lettering. Block capitals, clean, nothing like his, perfectly legible. 29TH ANNUAL CRAB DERBY. A crab: five legs. She's not an artist and doesn't care.

image.prompt: close-up of clean plain block-capital lettering on a flyer above a simple five-legged crab drawn without ceremony

panels.composition: WOOD in the door, late, hair flat on one side from sleep. Looking at the flyer. Looking at Maria.

balloons.text: It's February. You were asleep. It needed lettering.

image.prompt: a thin man with sleep-flattened hair standing in a shop doorway looking at a pregnant woman who has finished lettering a flyer
image.notes: Maria says 'Arthur.' Her only time. It lands flat, practical, like everything she says.

panels.composition: Sixteen flyers. The sixteenth, hers. Wood pinning it himself, carefully, and stepping back farther than usual.

image.prompt: a row of sixteen crab flyers on a shingle wall, the newest lettered in a different plain hand, a thin man stepping back to look, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Maria letters it. Five legs. 'It's a flyer, Arthur.'
